level.label: Level {level}
calibrating.label: Calibrating
calibrating.hint: For the first three nights OpenHoop is still learning what is normal for you. Treat the score as an indication.
flag.clock-offset: The band's clock was ahead or behind on this day. Times may be shifted a little.
empty.title: No data yet
empty.body: Pair a band or pick the demo band in Settings.
sleep.noPeriods: No sleep was recorded for this day.
readiness.contributionsHint: Points above or below your own normal
readiness.howBody: Readiness compares your night with your own normal. Three signals count: your HRV (above your average is favourable), your sleep (the sleep score) and your resting heart rate (below your average is favourable). Each signal adds or costs points. Together they give a number from 0 to 100.
readiness.modelTitle: A fitted model, not a measurement
readiness.modelBody: The formula was fitted to the outputs of another product and may differ for you. Use the score to follow your own trend, not as a medical judgement.
trends.fewDays: There are {count} days of data. The rest follows as you keep wearing the band.
lock.open.body: The band is releasing its data.
lock.locked.title: The band is withholding its data
lock.locked.body: The band's firmware does not release its history to third-party apps. OpenHoop does not bypass this and never tries to. Your live heart rate still works.
lock.no-data.body: The band is not sending data yet. Wear it for a while and try again.
lock.unknown.body: OpenHoop does not know yet whether the band releases its data. A first sync will show.
danger.title: Dangerous actions
danger.intro: These actions can erase data on the band or reset it. They cannot be undone.
danger.dialogBody: You are about to run an irreversible action on the band. Type {command} to confirm.
pairing.prepareBody: Charge the band and put it next to your phone. Turn Bluetooth on.
pairing.oneBondTitle: A band belongs to one phone at a time
pairing.oneBondBody: If the band is still paired with another phone or app, OpenHoop cannot connect to it. On that phone open the Bluetooth settings, pick the band and choose Forget or Unpair. Wait a minute, then search for it here again.
pairing.scanNone: No bands found. Check that the band is charged and close by.
pairing.sinceTitle: Since when have you worn this band?
pairing.sinceBody: Readings from before this date are never stored. That keeps data from a previous owner or a second-hand band out of your archive.
pairing.sinceInvalid: Enter a valid date that is not in the future.
pairing.bondBody: OpenHoop now asks Android to pair with the band. Confirm the request on your phone.
settings.maxHrHint: Leave empty to use {value} bpm (208 minus 0.7 times your age).
settings.maxHrHintNoYear: Enter your birth year to get a default value.
settings.profileInvalid: Check your input: birth year between 1900 and this year, maximum heart rate between 120 and 230.
settings.sourceHint: The demo band is a simulation inside the app. Nothing goes over the network.
settings.ownerSince: You have worn the band since
settings.exportBody: Shares a zip with one CSV per table and a copy of the database, for example as a backup.
about.local: Everything stays on your phone: no account, no server, no network traffic.
about.disclaimer: OpenHoop is not a medical device. The values are meant for personal insight, not for diagnosing, treating or preventing any condition.
about.affiliation: OpenHoop is not affiliated with or endorsed by WHOOP. It is an independent open-source project for the WHOOP 5.0 / MG band.
selftest.intro: These checks run on this device, in a temporary encrypted database that is removed afterwards. Your own data is not touched.
sync.phase.probing: Checking whether the band releases its data…
sync.banner: Syncing in the background. You can keep using the app.
error.bluetoothUnavailable: Bluetooth is not available on this device. The emulator has no Bluetooth radio; a real phone does. Pick the demo band to use the app.
error.bluetoothOff: Bluetooth is off. Turn Bluetooth on and try again.
error.bluetoothPermission: OpenHoop needs permission to find and connect to nearby devices. Grant it in Android settings and try again.
error.bandNotFound: No band was found. Check that the band is charged, close by and not connected to another phone or app.
error.bondRefused: The band refused to pair. It is probably still paired with another phone or app. On that device open the Bluetooth settings and choose Forget or Unpair for the band, wait a minute and try again.
error.connectFailed: Connecting to the band failed. Move closer to the band and try again.
error.disconnected: The connection to the band dropped. Data received so far is saved; sync again to continue.
error.timeout: The band is not answering. Try again in a few seconds.
error.commandFailed: The band rejected a request. Try again.
error.storage: The database cannot be opened. OpenHoop deletes nothing; restart the app.
error.noBandPaired: No band is paired yet. Pair one on the Band tab, or pick the demo band in Settings.
error.busySyncing: A sync is running. Wait until it finishes, then start live heart rate.
error.shareUnavailable: Sharing is not available on this device.
danger.note: This version of OpenHoop has no code path that sends a write, dangerous or forbidden command to the band. The confirmation therefore does nothing.
pairing.lockedDone: Paired, but the band does not release its history.
settings.sourceUntested: The real band is untested: the bands have not arrived yet. Pick the demo band to use the app.
settings.exportWarning: The database copy inside the zip is not encrypted. Keep the zip safe. The database key is never included.
selftest.wrongKey: A wrong key does not open the database
error.ownerSinceMissing: OpenHoop doesn't know since when you have worn this band, so it won't sync. This keeps a previous owner's data out of your archive. Pair the band again via Band › Pair a band and enter the date there.
sync.stop.clock: The band's clock is wrong: it is not set, or it is more than two minutes off. OpenHoop therefore requested nothing and removed nothing from the band. The laptop workbench has an option to override this deliberately.
sync.stop.corrupt: A block of data kept arriving damaged. OpenHoop did not acknowledge that block, so it is still on the band. Everything received before it has been saved. Try again later with the band close to your phone.
settings.ownerLaterBody: You are choosing a later date. OpenHoop will delete all readings, events and log lines from before {date} and recompute your days. This cannot be undone. Raw blocks from the band are only kept whole, so a block that spans {date} stays and may still hold some readings from before it. Those no longer count anywhere.
notBuilt.title: Not built yet
notBuilt.body: This part of the design has no data behind it yet. Nothing here is a guess.
